title: Pair of Straight Lines
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: What is the combined (joint) equation of two lines u = 0 and v = 0?
cards.a: u · v = 0. A point (x, y) satisfies u · v = 0 iff it lies on line u = 0 OR line v = 0.
cards.hint: Any line pair equation factors into two linear equations.

cards.q: What does a homogeneous second-degree equation ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 represent?
cards.a: It always represents a pair of straight lines passing through the origin (0, 0).
cards.hint: Since degree of every term is 2, it is satisfied by (0, 0).

cards.q: Sum and product of slopes m₁, m₂ for ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0?
cards.a:
m₁ + m₂ = -2h / b
m₁ · m₂ = a / b.
cards.hint: Derived from the auxiliary equation: b m² + 2h m + a = 0.

cards.q: Condition for lines represented by ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 to be real/distinct, coincident, or imaginary?
cards.a:
Real & distinct: h² - ab > 0
Coincident (identical): h² - ab = 0
Imaginary (only origin): h² - ab < 0.
cards.hint: Discriminant Δ = 4(h² - ab) of the quadratic bm² + 2hm + a = 0 governs the nature.

cards.q: Acute angle θ between the lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0?
cards.a: tan θ = | 2 √(h² - ab) / (a + b) |.
cards.hint: Always take absolute value to ensure θ is acute (0 ≤ θ ≤ π/2).

cards.q: Condition for the lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 to be perpendicular?
cards.a: a + b = 0 (i.e. coefficient of x² + coefficient of y² = 0).
cards.hint: Most frequently asked MHT-CET property! Independent of the value of h.

cards.q: Condition for the lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 to be coincident / parallel?
cards.a: h² - ab = 0  (or h² = ab).
cards.hint: Lines passing through origin are parallel only when they coincide.

cards.q: Joint equation of the angle bisectors of ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0?
cards.a: (x² - y²) / (a - b) = xy / h  or  h(x² - y²) - (a - b)xy = 0.
cards.hint: Sum of coefficients of x² and y² is h + (-h) = 0, proving bisectors are always perpendicular.

cards.q: General second-degree equation representing a pair of straight lines?
cards.a: ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0.
cards.hint: Contains linear and constant terms, so the lines do not necessarily pass through the origin.

cards.q: Condition for general second-degree equation to represent a pair of straight lines?
cards.a: Δ = abc + 2fgh - af² - bg² - ch² = 0  AND  h² - ab ≥ 0.
cards.hint: Determinant form: | [a, h, g], [h, b, f], [g, f, c] | = 0.

cards.q: Coordinates of the point of intersection of ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0?
cards.a: (x, y) = ( (hf - bg) / (ab - h²), (gh - af) / (ab - h²) ).
cards.hint: Denominator is (ab - h²). Note: numerator signs: hf - bg and gh - af.

cards.q: 10-second shortcut to find point of intersection without memorizing formulas?
cards.a: Differentiate partially wrt x (set ∂f/∂x = 0) and wrt y (set ∂f/∂y = 0). Solve these two linear equations simultaneously!
cards.hint: 2ax + 2hy + 2g = 0 and 2hx + 2by + 2f = 0. Solving them gives the intersection point in seconds!

cards.q: Angle between lines for the general equation ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0?
cards.a: tan θ = | 2 √(h² - ab) / (a + b) |.
cards.hint: Angle depends ONLY on the second-degree coefficients a, h, b. Linear terms g, f, c have zero effect on angle!

cards.q: Condition for lines of general equation to be parallel?
cards.a: h² - ab = 0  AND  bg² = af² (or g² / a = f² / b).
cards.hint: Both conditions must hold for lines to be distinct parallel lines.

cards.q: Distance between two parallel lines represented by general second-degree equation?
cards.hint: Notice factor of 2 in front of the square root.

cards.q: Product of perpendicular distances from origin to ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0?
cards.a: p₁ · p₂ = |c| / √[ (a - b)² + 4h² ].
cards.hint: Standard MHT-CET formula. If lines pass through origin, c = 0 so product is 0.

cards.q: Product of perpendiculars from point (x₁, y₁) to ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0?
cards.a: p₁ · p₂ = |a x₁² + 2h x₁ y₁ + b y₁²| / √[ (a - b)² + 4h² ].
cards.hint: Denominator √[ (a - b)² + 4h² ] is identical to that in the angle bisector magnitude.

cards.q: Homogenization: How to find the joint equation of lines joining origin to points of intersection of a curve and a line lx + my + n = 0?
cards.a: Write the line as (lx + my) / (-n) = 1. Multiply linear terms of curve by ((lx + my)/(-n)) and constant term by ((lx + my)/(-n))² to make every term degree 2.
cards.hint: The resulting equation is homogeneous of degree 2 and represents the pair of lines through origin.

cards.q: Condition for lines joining origin to intersections of curve and line to be perpendicular?
cards.a: After homogenizing to Ax² + 2Hxy + By² = 0, set A + B = 0.
cards.hint: A + B = 0 is always the perpendicularity test for any homogeneous pair of lines.

cards.q: Area of triangle formed by lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 and the line lx + my + n = 0?
cards.a: Area = | (n² √(h² - ab)) / (a m² - 2h l m + b l²) |.
cards.hint: High-yield shortcut for MHT-CET triangle area MCQs.

cards.q: Lines parallel to ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 passing through point (x₁, y₁)?
cards.a: a(x - x₁)² + 2h(x - x₁)(y - y₁) + b(y - y₁)² = 0.
cards.hint: Shift origin to (x₁, y₁) by substituting x → x - x₁ and y → y - y₁.

cards.q: Condition that one line of ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 is perpendicular to line px + qy = 0?
cards.a: Slope of line is -p/q, so perpendicular slope is q/p. Substitute m = q/p into auxiliary equation: b(q/p)² + 2h(q/p) + a = 0 ⇒ b q² + 2h p q + a p² = 0.
cards.hint: Substitute the required slope directly into bm² + 2hm + a = 0.

cards.q: Condition that one line of ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 coincides with line y = mx?
cards.a: b m² + 2h m + a = 0.
cards.hint: m must be a root of the auxiliary equation.

cards.q: When does ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 represent the coordinate axes?
cards.a: When a = 0, b = 0, and h ≠ 0, giving the equation 2hxy = 0 ⇒ xy = 0.
cards.hint: xy = 0 factors into x = 0 (y-axis) and y = 0 (x-axis).

cards.q: Condition for the lines ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 to be equally inclined to coordinate axes?
cards.hint: If lines are equally inclined to axes, their slopes are m and -m (sum = 0).
